Saved Work Redesign

A reorganization of where users manage their files. Three zones replacing one chaotic list. Fixing 7 abandoned sections and bringing external workflows back inside the product.

The problem

A feature nobody used.

14 file types in one flat list. No filtering, no search, no context. Users couldn't find what they needed, so they kept a parallel Excel sheet to manage their work.

Pendo data showed 7 sections with under 2% usage. Research interviews confirmed: the structure didn't match how researchers actually think about their work.

"I have an Excel sheet next to my browser. Everything should just work inside your product."

Research participant · Contract researcher

The solution

Three zones instead of 14 types.

Reorganized around the way researchers actually describe their work: by project, not by file type. Each zone has its own rules, search, and actions.

The interface
Interface patterns & details

Before — the original Saved Work interface: a flat list spanning 14+ sections with minimal project context and no in-row actions.

Project Details — opening a saved project surfaces its full context: description, ownership, notes, attachments, and edit history.

What changed

Three distinct zones.

01 Core
Project Workspace

Active work. Files directly tied to the current project. Search, filter, and detail view built in. Where most actions happen.

02 Core
Repository

Templates, standards, and reference materials. Shared across projects. Lower friction to search across the org.

03 Core
Shared Folders

Collaboration across contracts. Visible in your org even when you switch projects. One place for handoffs.

04 New
Project Details

Metadata, team activity, and a live count of all content types. One place to see everything inside a project.

Impact

What the redesign changed.

Before
  • 14 file types in one flat list
  • No project context or filter
  • No search within sections
  • No metadata without opening the file
  • Actions hidden or duplicated
  • No sharing across contracts
  • Users keeping external Excel files
  • 7 sections with under 2% usage
After
  • Three zones: Workspace, Repository, Folders
  • Navigation filtered by active project
  • Search built into every section
  • Item detail panel always visible
  • Actions consolidated per type
  • Shared Folders visible across org
  • All work manageable in-product
  • Sections restructured by actual workflow

Next steps

Two directions we considered.

Option A: Recommended
Ship this redesign first

Immediate improvement. Generates real usage data to scope the larger Project Management build.

  • Ship Saved Work redesign
  • Observe adoption patterns
  • Scope Project Management from data
  • Migrate gradually, lower risk
Option B
Skip to full rebuild

Given low usage, skip the interim fix and invest directly in the full Project Management system.

  • Skip this redesign
  • Define full PM scope
  • Build and ship new core flow
  • Full migration required

Decision pending — depends on migration feasibility and engineering capacity.

Reflection

What I learned.

What worked

Auditing all 14 file types before touching the solution. The three-zone rail came from how researchers describe their work, not file types. Pendo data gave us a shared starting point. Two concrete roadmap options made the strategic conversation possible.

Still open

Roadmap decision pending. Cross-contract sharing needs legal review. Project Details needs usability testing. Large-portfolio users (100+ items) not yet tested.
